findings.fix: Escalate before declaring no way on: dead ends up to 3 rounds (30 searches), then walls up to 4 rounds, closest to the biggest unexplored region first.

findings.title: Known traps count as walls, and trap doors are never used as a way down
findings.problem: View.walkable returns False for every trap (line 129). A squeaky board or arrow trap in a one-wide corridor or doorway seals off the rest of the level, and a known trap door or hole, which is a free way down, is ignored.
findings.evidence: Traps sit in the explored area of no-way-on snapshots B19492907 (sleeping gas trap), B19584112 (two bear traps) and B20313006 (arrow and teleport traps).
findings.fix: Make low-risk traps (squeaky board, arrow, dart, rust, rolling boulder) walkable at a higher path cost. Use 'trap door' or 'hole' as a go_down target when no stairs can be reached.

findings.title: RuleBrain orders a fight with shopkeepers, watchmen and ghosts
findings.problem: Any 'X adjacent, difficulty N > limit' escalation becomes fight {target: X} (lines 47-49). That includes an angry shopkeeper (difficulty 15) and watchmen, and Elbereth does not stop @-humans or shopkeepers either.
findings.evidence: 7 stalls read 'shopkeeper adjacent, difficulty 15 > N (last order: fight shopkeeper)'. Replaying B20234314, B20015104 and B20061114 with the current code attacks the shopkeeper at 7/37, 14/43 and 15/56 HP.
findings.fix: Never fight shopkeepers, watchmen, priests or guards. For an angry shopkeeper, pay with 'p' if gold allows (that calms him), otherwise leave by the nearest stairs or pray. For monsters over difficulty that are not @, step_away or elbereth first.

findings.title: 'Eat the fresh kill' sends e when no corpse is there and leaves a pack prompt open
findings.problem: _corpse_to_eat (lines 902-907) sends 'e' on the kill square without checking a corpse is there; small monsters often leave none. The pack prompt that follows ('What do you want to eat? [d or ?*]') is handled in mechanics only when declined_corpse is set (lines 334-336), so it goes to the brain. eating_corpse also stays True, and the kill record stays.
findings.evidence: B20323702 stalled on "prompt: yn 'What do you want to eat? [d or ?*]'" straight after 'You kill the jackal!' and 'standing order: eat the fresh kill'.
findings.fix: Send 'e' only if the square showed a corpse cell before the hero stepped on it, or a 'You see here ... corpse' message came in. In mechanics, if eating_corpse is set and the prompt starts 'What do you want to eat', send ESC, clear the flag and pop the kill.

findings.title: The corpse diet is narrow and kill records miss most kills
findings.problem: SAFE_CORPSES (lines 43-49) leaves out common safe early corpses: hobbit, dwarf, dwarf lord and dwarf king (for non-dwarves), Woodland-elf, Green-elf and Grey-elf (for non-elves), giant ant, garter snake and grid bug. _record_kills (lines 874-885) credits a kill only when pending_fight is set, so kills by thrown daggers or the pet are lost, and 'You kill it' becomes '?'. FRESH_TURNS=30 is stricter than needed; about 40 is still safe.
findings.evidence: Together with the missing packed foods, this is why 80 games reach Weak with nothing to eat. The Weak snapshots average about 4500 turns, and most are on Dlvl 2-3.
findings.fix: Extend the list with race-aware kin checks. Record kills from thrown weapons at the square that was targeted. Accept lichen and lizard corpses anywhere, regardless of who killed them.

findings.title: No progress watchdog: the pilot loops for thousands of turns with stairs known
findings.problem: _default_activity has no check that the dungeon level or the explored area changes over time. Only the per-key _stuck_guard exists, and it misses loops of different keys.
findings.evidence: B20313002 sat on Dlvl2 until T10509 with two staircases down known at (20,4) and (69,13). Its feed alternates 'go down: head for the stairs down' and 'search walls: go search near (8,18)' next to a shop door until the hero goes Weak. Three games hit the 20000-turn limit on Dlvl2.
findings.fix: Track turns since the last new dlvl or new explored square. After about 1500 turns with stairs known, force go_down (fight whatever is in the way); with no stairs, escalate once with the loop as the reason.

findings.title: Thrown daggers ignore pets and peacefuls in the line of fire
findings.problem: r_throw (lines 626-633) picks any monster cell whose name matches, peaceful or not, and fires down the line without checking for the pet, a peaceful or a wall between. Hitting the pet turns it hostile; hitting a peaceful angers it and costs alignment.
findings.evidence: Inference: 4 deaths to domestic animals (kitten 2, little dog, pony). In B20313003 a hostile kitten sat next to a floating eye and a yellow mold, the kinds of targets ranged_kill throws at.
findings.fix: Take the target from visible_hostiles, which excludes peacefuls, and walk the line square by square, refusing if a pet, peaceful or wall comes before the target.

findings.title: Message-driven logic misses messages that arrive with --More--
findings.problem: aipipe clears its message buffer on every snapshot (aipipe.c emit_state, nmsgs = 0), and mechanics() returns early on 'more' snapshots, so routines only see messages from the final command snapshot. That affects door state and the shop sign (lines 419-427), smudged engravings (line 592) and the corpse check (line 903). _default_activity also runs r_loot before r_explore, so the door checks are skipped on any step where loot acts.
findings.evidence: 'Closed for inventory' was on screen in B20313001, yet the next door was kicked anyway. Some of the 5 elbereth-stuck snapshots end with 'Never mind.' after an aborted engrave, with no handler seeing why.
findings.fix: In Engine.step, keep appending messages to memory.recent_msgs on every snapshot, and clear the list after the first command snapshot has been processed. Message checks read recent_msgs, and the door and shop checks run before r_loot.

findings.title: Batch data loses its diagnostics, and scenario replays overwrite the stall snapshots
findings.problem: Engine stats (turns by activity, corpses eaten and declined, throws, prayers, waits) only go to stdout; the CSV drops them (cols at lines 490-491). finish() records maxlvl as the current dlvl for stalls. Game.play writes batch/<name>.json on any stall, so a scenario replay overwrites the original snapshot.
findings.evidence: batch/B20234307.json says 'Weak' at T1463, but the CSV and scenarios/B20234307.json say 'brain loop: small mimic' at T1165. Turn-sink questions (resting, searching, waiting) cannot be answered from saved data.
findings.fix: Add a stats column (JSON) to the CSV or write per-game stats JSON. Have scenario.run write to playground/replays/ instead of batch/. Track the deepest dlvl in the Game object.
